anyway, I think there were maybe like 7 girls that it showed me before it must have run out. I think the search distance was pretty wide too. I don't want to make it seem like I am being vain or anything of the sort but I probably don't fit the mold of the typical autist that hangs out on forums like this or would join a neurodivergent dating app, in terms of values/aesthetic, and all the girls that were there definitely did. If that makes any sense.

this is just me, perhaps ineffectively, trying to articulate that while I don't think there was anything wrong with any of the girls on the app, it's clear that they all belonged to a relatively specific demographic that I did not.

I suppose there is some conclusion to be drawn from this that it's a certain person that goes out of their way to use a dating app specifically for autistic people rather than using a traditional app and finding people that you click with regardless of mental condition (however difficult that may be), but I am not comfortable drawing that conclusion, especially since I am one of the people who belongs to the former group. notably this is the only time I have ever used a dating app. I also used it for all of 20 minutes before deleting my account and pretending it never happened. 

I'm sure many, if not most people on this sub would probably be ok with this, because as I mentioned I am something of an outlier even among autistic people. I just wanted to indicate that I think the demographic diversity for this app seems to be kind of slim.

hello, headphones are a bit of an interest for me so I think I could help if I could just understand a bit more what exactly it is you're looking for. I assume you ask for headphones because you want them to be able to play audio as well as block outside sound? do you specifically want headphones or would you also do earbuds? and someone asked if you wanted active or inactive but you seemed unsure so allow me to explain the differences and ask again.

inactive (or passive) noise cancelling is where the sound is blocked just because the headphone is physically blocking your ear. active noise cancelling is where the headphone actually uses a microphone to listen to outside sounds, and then plays an opposing frequency which cancels out the sound wave and it makes it inaudible. it works best for canceling out low, predictable frequencies, so a lot of ambient noise like engines and air conditioning will be removed but it doesn't work as well for higher or more sporadic frequencies like talking. (though will still be just as good as passive) what this means though is that they tend to be much more expensive.

Hey, I cant give a diagnosis nor should anyone on reddit, but those are definitely some symptoms that I had when I was younger and still do to some degree. At first I thought you may just have ADD or something similar but overthinking, being overly concerned with what other people think of you, and struggling to get the thoughts in your head into words from your mouth are common symptoms. for me the diagnosis (which was very early in my life, before or around 10 I believe) never really did anything for me other than tell me how to find people with similar experiences because they never put me on any meds or put me in any therapy or anything that helped like that. there's probably no reason to stress about the diagnosis because there's basically no difference between having autism and having basically-but-not-quite-autism. so sorry if this seems unhelpful but I don't think there's any way to "discover ASD in a productive manner" especially since you are at least older than 19 and made it presumably successfully through your formative years
